title: A Japanese Chef Spent 15 Years Perfecting Biryani. Tokyo's Michelin Guide Noticed.
excerpt: Chef Takamasa Osawa's 10-seat biryani restaurant in Tokyo earned a Bib Gourmand in the Michelin Guide Tokyo 2026, making it only the second biryani-focused establishment globally to receive Michelin recognition.
body:
• Chef Takamasa Osawa's Biryani Osawa in Tokyo earned a Bib Gourmand in the Michelin Guide Tokyo 2026, becoming only the second biryani restaurant globally to receive Michelin recognition.
  • Osawa spent 15 years traveling across India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh to perfect the dish after a life-changing trip to Tamil Nadu, eventually opening a reservations-only 10-seat restaurant in Tokyo.
  • The only other biryani restaurant with Michelin recognition is Singapore's Bismillah Biryani, which holds nine Bib Gourmand nods — biryani's heartlands of India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh have no Michelin Guide coverage at all.
  • Osawa recently cooked biryani at the Hyderabad home of Tollywood star Ram Charan, calling the city a continuing education in the dish.

From Tamil Nadu to Tokyo

Takamasa Osawa's path to becoming one of the world's most recognized biryani chefs began with an unlikely detour. A trip to Tamil Nadu years ago left the Japanese chef so captivated by the layered rice dish that he spent the next 15 years crisscrossing India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh, studying regional variations from Hyderabadi dum to Lucknowi to Kolkata-style biryani.

The result is Biryani Osawa, a reservations-only, 10-seat counter-style restaurant in Tokyo where the chef prepares a single dish with the precision Japanese cuisine is known for and the depth of flavour that biryani demands. In the Michelin Guide Tokyo 2026, the restaurant earned its first Bib Gourmand — a designation recognizing high-quality meals at moderate prices.

It is only the second biryani-focused restaurant in the world to receive Michelin recognition.

A Global Biryani Milestone

The first — and until now, only — biryani restaurant in the Michelin universe is Singapore's Bismillah Biryani, which holds nine Bib Gourmand nods accumulated over the years. In a blog post acknowledging Osawa's achievement, Bismillah wrote: "That biryani is now earning Michelin recognition in Japan speaks volumes. This is a dish that was born on the subcontinent, carried across oceans, and is now inspiring chefs in the most unexpected corners of the world to stake their name on it."

"Today I cooked biryani in a private home. Grateful for the trust. This city keeps teaching me what biryani is."

— Chef Takamasa Osawa, on Instagram after cooking for Ram Charan in Hyderabad

The Bib Gourmand is a step below Michelin's coveted star ratings, but it carries significant weight in the food industry — particularly for a dish that has never been represented in the guide's highest tiers. Biryani's heartlands — India, Pakistan, Bangladesh — have no Michelin Guide coverage at all, making the recognition of biryani in Tokyo a notable footnote in the ongoing globalization of Indian cuisine.

Cooking for Tollywood Royalty

Osawa's reputation has extended well beyond Tokyo's food scene. In late 2025, the chef traveled to Hyderabad — arguably the biryani capital of the world — to cook at the home of Tollywood superstar Ram Charan and his wife, Upasana Konidela. The private gathering at the family's Jubilee Hills residence saw Osawa prepare biryani outdoors in the traditional style.

Ram Charan described the meal as "flavourful." Osawa, reflecting on the experience, wrote on Instagram that the city keeps teaching him what biryani is — a statement that underscores the humility that has defined his 15-year journey with the dish.

The Restaurant Experience

At Biryani Osawa, every detail reflects the intersection of Japanese culinary discipline and South Asian tradition. Diners sit at a counter, watching the chef prepare each pot. The menu is focused: biryani, a spicy sauce, raita, and a spiced vanilla bean ice cream dessert. Reviewers describe perfectly balanced spices, aromatic rice, and a clean presentation that sets the restaurant apart from the more rustic environments where biryani is traditionally served.

The restaurant carries a near-perfect rating on review platforms, with diners from South Asia frequently commenting that Osawa's version is among the best they have tasted anywhere — a striking endorsement for a Japanese chef cooking a quintessentially South Asian dish.

What It Means for Indian Cuisine Abroad

Osawa's Michelin recognition arrives at a moment when Indian food is experiencing unprecedented global visibility. From biryani franchises expanding across America to dosa pop-ups in European capitals, the Indian culinary footprint is growing. But Michelin recognition has remained elusive for most Indian restaurants, and the absence of the guide from India itself means the cuisine's finest expressions go unrated by the world's most influential dining authority.

That a Japanese chef earned biryani its second-ever Michelin nod is both a tribute to the dish's universal appeal and a reminder that the global recognition of Indian cuisine remains a work in progress — one that may ultimately be judged from places far from where the food was first cooked.
nri_angle: The Michelin recognition of a biryani restaurant in Tokyo highlights both the global spread of Indian cuisine and the absence of Michelin coverage from India's own culinary heartlands.
